transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining the pre-approval huddle for our middle-school mathematics assessment scheduled for May 14, 2027. I've reviewed the draft administration plan, which calls for digital testing on school tablets, all 26 students testing together in Room 201, one proctor, graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, and completed materials stored in the general records cabinet. Before I give my final approval, I'd like each of you to review the draft and raise any concerns you see from your respective areas. Let's start with the testing coordinator — does anything stand out to you?

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I have a significant concern with the draft plan. The state administration manual limits a testing room to 14 students, but the draft calls for all 26 students testing together in Room 201. I've already prepared the rooms to comply with state rules: Room 201 is set up for 14 students and Room 202 for 12 students. Additionally, state testing supervision rules require one proctor assigned to each testing room, so we need two proctors — not one. I should also note that the updated room plan has not yet been entered into the district tracker.

When I reviewed the current state mathematics assessment manual this week, I found that calculators may be used only on section 2 of the assessment and must be four-function calculators. The draft plan currently calls for graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, which would violate state guidelines. We need to revise the plan to specify four-function calculators restricted to section 2 only.
